title: Runtime attention scheduler experimentation harness for heterogeneous kernels
creator: Nisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build an experimentation harness and incremental rollout plan for a runtime scheduler that chooses among heterogeneous attention kernels (FlashAttention v2, FlashAttention v3, our legacy kernels, and a lightweight quantized kernel) at request granularity. The scheduler must consider sequence length, batch shape, per-head precision, hardware topology (A100/H100/MIG partitions), and prefill vs decode phase constraints.

Background: Our serving runtime currently selects kernels via a static heuristic tuned for average workloads. Recent model variants (long-context and multi-precision) show divergent performance characteristics: FA3 has better long-sequence throughput but exhibits higher jitter during short decode loops in some driver/kernel combinations. Several customer regressions were traced to kernel-selection thrashing during prefill->decode transitions.

Scope: 1) Instrumented microbenchmark harness (GPU-local) to exercise combinations of kernels and input shapes; 2) Runtime scheduler prototype with pluggable scoring functions and hysteresis; 3) Canary plan for canarying scheduler on dedicated pools with traffic shadowing; 4) Telemetry and SLO tests for tail latency, p50/p95 token latency, and token cost delta.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: full rollout automation, RBAC changes for Private deployments, and model-level AI-driven cost-optimization (later follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible microbenchmark matrix that measures per-kernel latency and memory footprint across sequence lengths 8..32768 and batch sizes 1..16
A runtime scheduler binary flag + config that can be toggled per-deployment and supports weighted scoring functions and hysteresis windows
A canary run (at least one week) with traffic shadowing to >=1% of production for a non-critical model showing no >5% regression in p95 decode token latency
Dashboards showing kernel-switch counts, scheduler decisions, and token-level cost deltas for canary traffic
Fallback path: if the scheduler causes >6% tail-latency regression, automatic rollback to previous static heuristic succeeds without traffic loss
technical_notes: Scorer inputs: sequence_length, decode_step_time_budget, kv-cache-residency, model_quantized (bool), device_free_memory, sm_clock, head_count
Hysteresis proposal: sticky selection for N_decode_tokens=16 or 250ms whichever earlier; soft score delta threshold 7% to switch
Memory safety: verify workspace sizes across kernels at max_batch*max_seq + kv-cache and fall back to safe kernel on OOM
Prefill vs Decode: prefer low-latency kernel for first decode step after prefill when remaining_budget < 30ms
Metrics to emit: selected_kernel, score_vector, switch_cause (hysteresis|score_delta|resource_limit), kernel_latency_estimate, observed_decode_token_us
decisions: Use a pluggable scorer architecture instead of hardwired heuristics to allow A/B experiments and feature flags
Start with linear combination of normalized features (latency_estimate, memory_headroom, quant_penalty) rather than ML model for predictability
Enable hysteresis with two knobs: token_count_sticky and time_window_ms to reduce selection thrash during prefill->decode transitions
Canary will use dedicated GPU pool with mirrored traffic (shadow mode) to avoid user-facing risk
comments: 2026-02-22 - Nisha Patel: Project created after postmortem of regression on model X. Initial design doc linked. Asked ENG infra to reserve a small H100 pool for canary experiments.

2026-03-02 - Owen Martinez: Prototype scorer implemented (branch: feat/attn-scheduler-proto). Microbench harness added to internal perf repo. Initial microbench shows FA3 wins at seq>2048 for batch 1, FA2 beats for short seq decode loops.

2026-03-07 - Lina Chen (SRE): Observed kernel-switch thrash in synthetic long->short workload; producing ~6-9% p95 tail increase due to context warmup. Proposed hysteresis fix and sticky affinity per request.

2026-03-10 - PR review: @backend-team reviewed scorer config schema; suggested adding explicit score weights in runtime config and a safety cap for kernel switches per-request (suggested 3 switches max).

2026-03-12 - Canary kickoff: Shadowing enabled for model: experimentation-chat-1 on devdedicated-3, ~1.2% traffic. Early telemetry: kernel_switch_count increased x1.8 compared to baseline and p95 decode token latency +3.8% (within threshold).

2026-03-14 - Observed regression spike from a driver edge-case when FA3 tried to allocate workspace during bursty prefills. Applied temporary runtime gate to prefer legacy kernel for prefills when device_free_memory < 12GB. Next step: add memory-aware scoring and bump hysteresis token_count to 32.
mitigations: Shadow traffic canary and short canary windows before unblocking
Automatic rollback trigger on >6% p95 token latency regression or error-rate increase
Per-model opt-out toggle so customers can pin to legacy heuristic during Private deployments
Add deterministic unit tests for scorer and simulated switch sequences to detect thrash patterns
